feasibility_reasoning:
The main claim holds. The entry imports only createClient from vendor-supabase (`import{c as e0}from"./vendor-supabase-Pf0Abwmk.js"`, source src/integrations/supabase/client.ts:14), and no other boot chunk imports that chunk (vendor-radix-boot imports only vendor-react). So a facade does take 224 KB raw / 58.6 KB transfer out of the boot closure. Guests keep working because AuthProvider settles through getSession() (src/hooks/useAuth.tsx:358). Realtime only runs for signed-in users (CommentsSection.tsx:118), and 786 test files mock the client export, so both stay intact. The change as written is incomplete, though:
(a) client.ts:35-39 keeps detectSessionInUrl at its default with the implicit flow (auth-js/dist/module/lib/constants.js:21). Magic-link, OAuth and password-recovery landings carry their tokens in location.hash and have nothing in storage, so the guest facade never loads the SDK. AuthFormBlocks.tsx:1109-1114 then waits for PASSWORD_RECOVERY forever, and those logins never take effect.
(b) vite.config.ts:353 sends every @supabase/* module to vendor-supabase, so import('@supabase/postgrest-js') loads the full 224 KB chunk, not ~8 KB. vite.config.ts is not in the file list.
(c) tslib sits inside vendor-supabase, and vendor-radix-CIuvgUd0.js statically imports {_,a,b} from it. Guests load vendor-radix after boot, so they still fetch and evaluate the SDK.
(d) src/lib/admin/community.ts:124 changes a builder in place (`query.ilike(...)` without reassigning), so the chain recorder must be mutable.
(e) The SSR branch must not keep a static supabase-js import in client.ts: auth-js, postgrest-js and realtime-js have no sideEffects:false, so the edge would survive in the client build.
blocking_issues: Implicit-flow URL tokens are ignored by wantsFull(), which only checks real || hasStoredAuthSession. Magic-link, OAuth and password-reset landings (AuthFormBlocks.tsx:1109-1114, LoginPopup.tsx:175, ClubAccessGate.tsx:323, GuestCheckoutGate.tsx:89) never establish a session. Fix: also load the SDK when location.hash or location.search contains access_token, refresh_token, error_description, code or type=.

vite.config.ts:353 puts postgrest-js in vendor-supabase, so the guest 'postgrest-only ~8 KB' chunk is really the full 224 KB SDK. It needs its own manualChunk and a check:chunks rerun; vite.config.ts is missing from the file list.

tslib is bundled into vendor-supabase, and vendor-radix statically imports it from there. Guests load vendor-radix after boot (prod 3881 ms), so the SDK is still downloaded and evaluated, and the check 'no vendor-supabase request for guests' fails. Fix: a separate tslib chunk, or C8.
The chain recorder must change the builder in place and return the same object: src/lib/admin/community.ts:124 calls query.ilike() without reassigning.

The server branch of client.ts must not keep a static @supabase/supabase-js import. auth-js, postgrest-js and realtime-js lack sideEffects:false, so the client build would keep the edge. Use a .server module or createIsomorphicFn.
effect_reasoning:
I ran the Lantern what-if (lighthouse-analyst/whatif.py on lha1 artifacts, h2 parity); its results are reproducible, with no CPU noise. Mobile base is 65: FCP 3974 / LCP 4819 / TBT 356 ms. Dropping vendor-supabase gives FCP 3823 (-151 ms), LCP 4518 (-301 ms), TBT 363 ms (+7) and perf 67. Adding the CPU actually attributable to the SDK (shrinkurl 0.85, which removes 29 ms observed, matching bootup scripting of 87-152 ms simulated, i.e. 22-38 ms observed) gives TBT 349 ms and perf still 67. Desktop at x1: FCP/LCP -40 ms, score stays 99. Desktop at x4 (the PSI proxy): FCP -40, LCP -60 ms, TBT 444 -> 499 ms with bytes only (moving FCP earlier pulls tasks into the TBT window) or 457 ms with the CPU removal; perf 79 -> 77..79. On top of C3: TBT 885 -> 829 ms, perf 78 -> 79.
So the claim of '-0.3 s FCP/LCP/SI' is right for LCP only. FCP is -0.15 s (about 2.7 ms/KB, because the chunk downloads in parallel with others). SI is about 0 on PSI: SI = max(FCP, 1.4*obsSI + 0.4*layoutSI), and the unthrottled obsSI barely moves. The 'bootup -57..-130 ms' figure is LH bootup time, not TBT; TBT changes by about 0.
On PSI the analyst infers that observed LCP comes after DCL, so the post-boot wave is inside the LCP set. Issues (b) and (c) bring vendor-supabase back into that wave, so the PSI LCP saving is between 0 and -0.3 s.
corrected_estimate: Mobile: +1 to +2 points standalone. On the fixture 65 -> 67. On PSI, FCP -0.15 s is about +0.5 point and LCP 0 to -0.3 s at 6.6 s is about +0 to +0.7 point. Desktop: 0 points (-2 to 0 on the x4 proxy). TBT: about 0 +/- 15 ms. SI: about 0 on PSI. With C3 the bytes no longer matter and the gain is about +1 point mobile (TBT -56 ms). The boot reduction of 58.4 KB gz is real only once the vendor-postgrest and tslib chunk fixes land.
better_alternative: Drop the postgrest-only path. Load the full SDK lazily on the first from/rpc/non-trivial auth call, and keep the guest getSession/onAuthStateChange short-circuit plus a URL-token check. That moves the same bytes out of pre-FCP, and therefore earns the same score, because the GoTrue CPU it would also save is worth about 0 TBT. It also avoids the second-client and header-parity risk. If the goal is bytes before FCP, C5 (dictionary split, -26 KB; what-if FCP -300 / LCP -151 ms, low risk) is better value per KB, and C3 makes both irrelevant for FCP/LCP.
